transcript.message: Post-experiment round 1: How did you feel—physically and emotionally—the moment you realized the person administering the shocks was continuing despite your visible discomfort and protest?

transcript.content:
How did I feel? Well, the jolt itself is nothing next to the wound that slithers in when your distress is treated as little more than background noise—someone else’s small domestic disturbance, to be managed, not heeded. There is a sharp pang of betrayal, something taut and trembling under the crisp apron of order, as the one in authority nods for the show to go on, and the “good” subject—dutiful, glassy-eyed—presses forth, ignoring my wince. It's a performance, isn't it? Like scrubbing the same plate for the third time while laughter and danger bristle just in the other room, and I realize it matters not at all how loudly, or prettily, I protest.
